### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4049efa34584a18485ccd13efcf4351f509205eb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a8e485cacd722ffc9b31133cca6bd08d5b1bd4b5` — the merge of head `365a6e4830fd27520c07daee7f1de542a2e77121` into base `4049efa34584a18485ccd13efcf4351f509205eb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a8e485cacd722ffc9b31133cca6bd08d5b1bd4b5 && git checkout a8e485cacd722ffc9b31133cca6bd08d5b1bd4b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4049efa34584a18485ccd13efcf4351f509205eb 365a6e4830fd27520c07daee7f1de542a2e77121 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4049efa34584a18485ccd13efcf4351f509205eb && git merge --no-ff 365a6e4830fd27520c07daee7f1de542a2e77121

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4049efa34584a18485ccd13efcf4351f509205eb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4049efa34584a18485ccd13efcf4351f509205eb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `75bff196c79ecae58c0cf8ebc5eb1f53ea97ac61`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-field-group-visibility-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts (`ObjectFieldGroupSchema.visibleWhen`), packages/spec/src/data/field-group-layout.ts, ui/packages/plugin-form/src/fieldGroups.ts (`visibleWhenFault: 'hidden'`), ui/packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx (`isFailClosedSectionGate` / `sectionGateVisible`), ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx (the `group` section reference), packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts (`recordsOf`), packages/qa/dogfood/test/expression-conformance.ledger.ts (`cel-field-group-section`), docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md (addendum of 2026-08-28), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`no-migration-prescription`). The two prose faces (content/docs/ui/field-grouping-and-order.mdx, .changeset/26646-field-group-visible-when-judged.md) are read for ② and the docs claim, not reviewed.

Card #26646 (body, triage `6441442924`, retriage `6445801471` / `6446746341`, claim `6453045956`, dev report `6454514811`), PR #26928 (body, 8 files, net diff vs `main` at merge-base `1708115e`) and the head's check-runs were the inputs. The PR body's account was not taken on trust; every claim below is read off the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set change (the narrowing), right.** `runStackExpressionPasses` gains one loop after the field walk of the object walk: for every `fieldGroups[]` entry it computes `fieldRuleRootVerdict('field group visibleWhen', raw)` and then `check(where, raw, objectName, 'record', verdict !== null)`, pushing the root verdict as `expression-invalid` at `error`. That is byte-for-byte the call pair the field triad loop makes for `visibleWhen` (`fieldRuleRootVerdict(key, raw)` + `check(where, raw, objectName, 'record', verdict !== null)`), so the group predicate is judged by exactly the field `visibleWhen` rules: it parses, reads `record.FIELD` and never a bare field, names a field the object declares (the object's columns alone, no `attachedOnRead` block, since the group is not a `SERVED_ROW_SITES` entry), calls only registered functions, and reads no root outside `FIELD_RULE_BOUND_ROOTS` (`record`, `previous`, `parent`). None of the write-path gates (the `parent` gate, the `requiredWhen` null guard, the traversal refusal) is applied, which matches the field `visibleWhen` slot (they are applied to `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen` only). Not fenced on `runtimeWriteType === 'object'`, so the object save door, draft promotion and the build give one finding. Right.
- **Scope of fields a group predicate may reference: right.** The predicate is checked against the whole object's field index, not the group's members. That is what the renderer evaluates: `sectionGateVisible` calls `evalFieldPredicate(f.visibleWhen, ruleRecord, false, previousRecord, predicateScope)` with the same `ruleRecord` (every declared field seeded) and the same host scope the field's own `visibleWhen` gets, so a group may read any declared field, and `previous`. Same binding, same rules.
- **Location `object 'NAME' · field group 'KEY' visibleWhen`: right.** It follows the `KIND 'NAME' SLOT` shape of its siblings in the same walk (`field 'X' visibleWhen`, `field 'X' option 'v' visibleWhen`, `action 'X' visible`, `validation 'X'`), keyed by the group's `key`, which is the name a field's `group` and a layout section's `group` point at. The order pin in `runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts` fixes its position after the option site and before the actions, at build and door alike.
- **Public surface.** No export is added or changed; `FIELD_GROUP_VISIBLE_WHEN_SLOT` is module-private, `fieldRuleRootIssue`'s signature is unchanged and its message for the four existing slots is byte-identical (the new branch is keyed on the slot name). `FIELD_RULE_SLOT_CONSEQUENCE` gains one cell. Right.
- **Corpus: measured as the dev says.** `fieldGroups` is declared on exactly four objects outside tests and the spec/lint/ui packages: `examples/app-showcase/.../contact.object.ts` (4 groups), `semantic-zoo.object.ts` (2, one carrying `icon`/`description`/`collapse`), `packages/create-objectstack/.../note.object.ts` (1), `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` scaffold (1). None carries a `visibleWhen`; `packages/platform-objects/src` declares no `fieldGroups` at all (its hits are generated translation bundles). 8 groups on 4 objects, 0 findings. Right.
- **#5017 receiver scan kept whole.** `obj.fieldGroups`, `fieldGroup.key`, `fieldGroup.visibleWhen` are literal member reads; `validate-expressions.test.ts` adds `fieldGroups` to the `obj` receiver's expected set and a `fieldGroup` receiver pinned to `ObjectFieldGroupSchema` through `shapeKeysOf` (the schema is a `lazySchema`). Right.
- **Dogfood conformance ledger.** `cel-field-group-section` classifies the slot by its evaluator and fail policy (`fail-closed`, renderer), as `cel-field-rule` does for the field slots without naming lint; nothing there becomes stale.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/26646-field-group-visible-when-judged.md` is in the root `.changeset/`, `'@objectstack/lint': minor`. The diff moves one published package (`@objectstack/lint`; `metadata-protocol` gains a test only), and the kind is `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a value an author could write is now refused), which takes at least `minor` under the Post-Task rule. Right.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both; the `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING, and the body carries the `**BREAKING**` banner with Before / Now / Unchanged. The triage's `yes (narrowing)` spelling is the malformed arm; the claim corrected it to `no (narrowing)`. Right.
- ADR-0087 marker: exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The gate refuses that category only when the body carries a FROM → TO prescription; the body carries none (no `FROM` token, no arrow, a `**The remedy.**` label, which `findMigrationPrescription`'s label branch does not match) and no key is added, removed or renamed, so the category is honest. `Check Changeset`, the job that runs `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset` and `check-adr-0087-registration --base MERGE_BASE`, concluded `success` on this head. Right.
- Title `fix(lint)!:` carries the bang. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: none raised; `open_questions: []`; `out_of_scope_findings` says only that no other group slot carries an expression (`ObjectFieldGroupSchema` confirms: `key`, `label`, `icon`, `description`, `visibleWhen`, `collapse` and three deprecated booleans). Answered.
- Premise: re-measured by the dev on `031d97a0` (200 / 422 / 422), consistent with the mechanism I read on `main` (no `fieldGroups` read anywhere in `validate-expressions.ts` before this diff). Answered.
- Skills-docs: `skills/**` never teaches `fieldGroups[].visibleWhen`; the docs page named is the one that gains the paragraph. Answered.
- Serial constraint #26847 (`validate-chart-bindings.ts`): disjoint from this diff's hunks; the head has `main` merged. Answered.
- Lane: `packages/lint` is `domain:spec` by the retriage answer; the PR touches `packages/lint` and a `metadata-protocol` test file only. Answered.
- `current_user` on a group is refused as on a field's `visibleWhen`, not as on an option's. That is the card's "same rules as field `visibleWhen`", and it is right for the slot: the renderer binds the group gate with the same `predicateScope` as the field's own rule (nothing server-side ever evaluates a group predicate), so the acceptance that per-option `visibleWhen` earns from the server's option check does not transfer. No escalation.

### ④ Design judgment

Read against the published spec on `main`: `ObjectFieldGroupSchema.visibleWhen` is declared as a CEL predicate "evaluated by the form renderer's section-gating contract against the record in scope: FALSE (or a faulting predicate, fail-closed) hides the WHOLE group, header included" (ADR-0085 addendum of 2026-08-28; `deriveFieldGroupLayout` passes it through verbatim; plugin-form stamps `visibleWhenFault: 'hidden'`; `form.tsx` takes a stamped divider off the fail-open triad and resolves it through `sectionGateVisible` with fallback `false`; the detail renderer's `group` section reference evaluates the same predicate and renders nothing when hidden).

- **Does the narrowing take a declared capability away?** No. The spec declares a CEL predicate over the record in scope; a predicate that cannot evaluate was never a capability, it was the spec's own refusal rendered as an invisible section. Every body the pass now refuses (unknown field, bare reference, unregistered function, syntax error, a root the renderer never binds) faulted at the renderer and hid the group for everyone on every form and record page. The one arguable case, `current_user` under a host that does bind it, is exactly the case the field `visibleWhen` slot already refuses for the same reason (display-only, no server evaluator, faults everywhere else), and the card asked for parity with that slot. The narrowing makes the spec's refusal real at authoring time, in the build and at the door, which is the ADR-0049 posture the schema's own history cites.
- **Fail-closed semantics in the message.** The group's consequence cell and the root-verdict opening are worded for the group ("binds only `record` …", "fails CLOSED: the whole group, header included, is hidden for everyone") and the field slots' wording is untouched; the pin asserts both. Right, and the direction matches `sectionGateVisible`'s fallback of `false`.
- **Try to break it.** (i) A group written with the `name` / `id` alias of `key` would locate at `field group '?'`; the strict schema refuses that body by name at the same door, so the location can only degrade on a body that is refused anyway. (ii) `recordsOf` reads the array shape the schema declares and the record shape its sibling rules tolerate, so a raw body at the door and the parsed body at the build walk the same entries. (iii) A stored sibling's broken group is not charged to this write (the door's differential, pinned). (iv) Draft save still lands and promotion is refused with the finding at the group's key (pinned through the real `saveMetaItem` / `publishMetaItem`); that is the existing draft-door contract for every other pass. (v) Order: build and door emit the group site after the option site and before the actions, pinned in the every-site body. Nothing broke.
- **Docs claim vs code.** The paragraph says the gate is fail-closed, whole section, header included; that `os validate`, `os build` and the save door judge it with the field `visibleWhen` rules; and that an unknown field is refused `expression-invalid` at the group's key. All three match the tree. One imprecision, should-fix 3 below.

Findings, none must-fix:

- **should-fix 1 — the user-root prescription is the field's, not the group's.** For `current_user` / `user` / `ctx` / `os` on a group, `fieldRuleRootIssue` appends the shared prescription, which opens with "To gate the CHOICES of a select by user, move the predicate to the option's own `visibleWhen` …" and continues "To hide the FIELD by role, declare field-level security …". A field group has no options and is not a field; the fitting prescription is the FLS clause (per field of the group) and the rewrite against `record`, which is what the changeset's `**The remedy.**` already says. Branch the prescription on `FIELD_GROUP_VISIBLE_WHEN_SLOT` as the opening sentence already is.
- **should-fix 2 — the receiver table in `validate-expressions.ts`'s header docblock is one row short.** It lists every read with the schema that declares it ("all verified against the live `.shape` in `validate-expressions.test.ts`"); the test now pins `objects[].fieldGroups` (`ObjectSchema`) and `fieldGroups[].key` / `.visibleWhen` (`ObjectFieldGroupSchema`), and the table does not.
- **should-fix 3 — docs: "a CEL predicate over `record`".** The check (and the renderer) also bind `previous` (and `parent` on a master-detail line item); the changeset's own Unchanged bullet accepts `previous.stage != record.stage`. Say so, or the page under-states what the gate accepts.

Check-runs on `75bff196c` as read at review time: 25 completed `success` (among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Build Docs, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size), 7 `skipped` (opt-in and matrix placeholders), 13 still `in_progress`: Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Test Core 1/8 – 8/8, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts for those families and are not pre-empted here; the dev's local run reports `@objectstack/lint` 170 files / 7485 tests and `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts` 218/218 at this head.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh` · 2026-10-27T22:31Z

Head `365a6e4830fd27520c07daee7f1de542a2e77121`. Card #26646 (triage `6441442924`, retriage answer `6446746341`: lane `domain:spec`), claim `6453045956`, dev report `6454514811`.

- **Contract review:** owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER on the `narrowing` face. The review (`6454674770`) at `75bff196` was a PASS with no must-fix. It found:
  - `fieldGroups[].visibleWhen` is judged with the same call pair as a field's `visibleWhen` (`fieldRuleRootVerdict` + the `record`-scoped `check`), not fenced on an object write. That is right for a group: the renderer's `sectionGateVisible` evaluates it in the same scope and fails closed, and nothing server-side evaluates it.
  - The location `object 'NAME' · field group 'KEY' visibleWhen` matches its siblings, and its order is pinned.
  - The corpus is 8 groups on 4 objects, none with `visibleWhen`, and `platform-objects` declares no groups, so nothing is refused.
  - The narrowing takes no declared capability away: every refused body faulted at the renderer and hid the group everywhere. It makes the spec's own fail-closed refusal real at authoring time.
- **Since then:** `365a6e48` closes all three should-fixes.
  - The group's user-root prescription now names FLS on a permission set or a rewrite against `record`, instead of the field's select-option wording, and the door test pins it.
  - The receiver table in the docblock of `validate-expressions.ts` gains the `fieldGroups` rows.
  - The docs name `previous`, and `parent` on a master-detail line item, beside `record`.
- **Shape:** `Fixes #26646`, 8 files, +397/−12. One root changeset, `@objectstack/lint` minor, with a BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` under a `**The remedy.**` label. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. `check-governed-merges --pr 26928`: NOT governed, 409 changed lines.
